newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks inch down in slow pre-FOMC trade.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks inch down in slow pre-FOMC trade.

text.p: Mexican stocks opened very slightly down in slow trade on Tuesday with the Dow Jones weighing on a thin-volume market awaiting the Federal Open Market Committee meeting to review U.S. interest rates, traders said.
"It's a very dull start and we expect the market to move sideways for the first few hours at thin volume until we know the outcome of the FOMC meeting," a floor trader said.
The leading IPC share index was off 0.65 points, or 0.02 percent, in the opening minutes of trade, at 3,920.73. Trading volume was wafer thin at 441,000 shares.
"Most stocks are following ADRs and the Dow (Jones)," another floor trader said.

Telmex weighed the market down most and accounted for 30 percent of shares traded in early dealing. Telmex stock was down six centavos to 17.12 pesos, shadowing its ADRs, which were off 1/4 to 43-1/4 in line with the Dow Jones.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average was meanwhile down 56.05 points at 7,172.83 points.
Media group Televisa headed the prominent gainers' list, up 2.30 pesos to 100.10 pesos.
"Televisa had been hit hard and was undervalued after being in the doldrums for several weeks," the floor trader added.

Dealers said Televisa also benefitted from buying ahead of a productivity plan the firm is expected to announce on Wednesday. Televisa was also bucking the downward trend among many other Mexican ADRs, and was ahead 3/8 to 25-3/8.

On the broad market, sliders outpaced gainers by 13 to seven, out of 39 stocks traded. Dealers said they expected the market to move little prior to the FOMC decision, expected slightly less than two hours before the close of trade.
